name: Citizenship by Marriage (Nacionalidad por Opción)

qualifying_event.description: A foreign spouse of a Peruvian citizen who has been continuously married for the required period and holds valid resident migratory status may apply for Peruvian citizenship by option, under Ley N.32421.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; proof of continuous marriage duration; valid resident status.

requirements.blocker_text: 4 years of continuous marriage to a Peruvian citizen before applying (raised from 2 years under the prior rule).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 4 years of continuous marriage to the Peruvian-citizen spouse.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must hold valid resident migratory status in Peru at the time of applying.
Same general examination applied to all naturalisation pathways: language, history, geography, Constitution, culture, and current affairs.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate showing 4 years' continuous marriage
Proof of valid resident migratory status

sources.title: El Peruano (Peru's official state gazette) -- Ley N.32421 extends the marriage-based citizenship pathway's continuous-marriage requirement from 2 to 4 years, requires valid migratory residency, and applies the same general exam requirement as other naturalisation pathways

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Peru). STATUS: DRAFT, LIVE LEGAL TRANSITION -- same caveat as pe_citizenship_naturalisation.json: El Peruano (tier-1) reports the marriage route now requires 4 years' continuous marriage under Ley N.32421, but a separate tier-3 source (tramitesperu.com) describes a still-active '2 years married + 2 years as Familiar de Residente' rule and frames Ley 32421 as pending its implementing regulation -- a direct, unresolved conflict between an official-gazette report and a practitioner report, disclosed rather than silently resolved. The economic/income requirement applied to standard naturalisation is NOT modeled here as a requirement, consistent with the tier-3 source's note that this pathway 'does not automatically grant citizenship' the way standard naturalisation's income test does -- though this distinction was not independently corroborated by the tier-1 source and should be treated cautiously.
